supersedes: data/xfv_lambda_parity_eval.json (the flat-curve stalemate this tournament resolves)
question: which lambda-SELECTION PROTOCOL generalizes best out-of-sample: the incumbent debuted-only selector (A), a production-parity selector (C globally-prepped / D per-fold-prepped), or frozen stamps (E)?

design.fold_2020: excluded as an eval fold (no prior fold for selection stability); its rows participate as training
design.selection: per eval fold Y and protocol P, run P's own internal machinery restricted to rows with decision_year < Y (band [0.50, 0.70] unchanged) -> lambda_P(Y)
design.evaluation: production blend at lambda_P(Y) on fold Y's debuted rows; production legs = efv_model.fit_production_stack fit on pre-Y rows (real decision years); cons floored at 0, model leg calibrated + clamped at -2.0
design.metrics: pooled Spearman + within-tier wm + FV-45 t45 (composite = sum, mirroring rank_calibration), plus contributor-AUC (>=3 WAR) and star-AUC (>=10 WAR) via source_backtest._auc

bootstrap.pairing: shared resample indices, paired diff vs protocol A on the pooled fold rows

protocols.A: incumbent (debuted-only anchor + ridge, raw model leg - the shipped rank_calibration selector)
protocols.C: parity, globally-prepped full pool (full-pool anchor, calibrated + clamped model leg)
protocols.D: parity, per-fold-prepped pool via fit_production_stack - LEAK-FIXED (see findings.lab_D_leakage)
protocols.E: null: frozen stamps as registered (hit 0.70 / pit 0.63)

registered_gates.gate1: composite (pooled+wm+t45) gap vs protocol A, pooled across folds, bootstrap lo95 >= 0
registered_gates.gate2: contributor-AUC and star-AUC each >= A - 0.005 pooled
registered_gates.ship_rule: challenger ships iff BOTH; if both C and D clear, higher composite wins; if neither clears, A is the adjudicated winner (valid no-loss outcome)

hit.note: parity is not merely non-superior on hitters - it is significantly WORSE (composite CI95 entirely negative) and fails the contributor-AUC floor (0.7626 < 0.7690 - 0.005)

pit.note: parity is a statistical tie on pitchers (point -0.0024, CI straddles 0); it clears the AUC floor but not the composite gate - no evidence it generalizes better

protocol_E_vs_A.question: is per-run re-selection adding anything over frozen stamps?
protocol_E_vs_A.hit: A per-fold re-selection beats frozen 0.70 by +0.0479 pooled composite but not significantly (lo95 -0.1155, p_gt_0 of E>A only 0.099 in E's favor is the mirror: re-selection is nominally better)
protocol_E_vs_A.pit: dead tie (E - A = +0.0039, CI [-0.0538, +0.0502]); at the ACTUAL current live stamp 0.61 (unregistered diagnostic E'), E' - A = -0.0011 - also a tie
protocol_E_vs_A.verdict: re-selection is not demonstrably adding value over frozen stamps, and is not hurting; no action indicated (E was a null arm, not a shippable challenger under the registration)

hit.note: argmax at the band cap - the standing near-boundary caveat continues to apply

pit.note: matches the CURRENT live stamp (data/xfv.json meta.live_lambda pit=0.61, stamped by the 2026-07-15 production run); the registration's 0.63 was the prior stamp

findings.lab_D_leakage: tools/xfv_lambda_parity_lab.py variant D filters raw matrix rows on r.get('decision_year') - a key the matrices DO NOT carry (decision year is computed, efv_model._decision_year) - so the filter is vacuous (2025/2025 pitcher rows pass a 'pre-2020' filter) and D's production stack was fit on ALL rows including each fold's own test rows. Leaky-D at HEAD selects hit 0.69 / pit 0.68; leak-fixed D selects hit 0.55 / pit 0.56.
findings.C_equals_D_when_leak_fixed: with the real decision-year filter, D produces fold rows IDENTICAL to C (same pool, same legs) - every per-fold selection, curve, and pooled composite matches C exactly. The 'two faithful parity implementations disagree at opposite ends of the band' conflict that motivated this adjudication was the leak artifact, not implementation sensitivity: there is exactly ONE faithful parity protocol, and it loses to the incumbent OOS.
findings.parity_artifact_stale_at_HEAD: data/xfv_lambda_parity_eval.json does not reproduce at HEAD f282695 on the committed matrices (all six variant curves differ; registered pit-A argmax 0.63 vs 0.61 at HEAD) - it was generated against an earlier code/matrix state and should be regenerated or marked superseded by this artifact.
findings.live_stamp_drift: blend_lambda live-computes rank_calibration each production run: the pit stamp had already moved 0.63 -> 0.61 in the 2026-07-15 run, independent of this adjudication. The E' diagnostic shows 0.61 is a tie with per-fold re-selection - the current stamp is well-supported.

verdict.winner: A (incumbent) - BOTH sides; no per-side split
verdict.stamps: stay on the incumbent selector's live output (hit 0.70 / pit 0.61 as of the 2026-07-15 run)
verdict.reason: neither challenger cleared gate 1 on either side (hit: parity significantly worse, lo95 -0.1842; pit: tie, lo95 -0.0274) and hit also failed the contributor-AUC floor. Per the pre-registered ship rule this is a clean adjudicated no-loss outcome: the debuted-only selector is not a documented quirk to be repaired - it is the OOS-winning protocol.
verdict.closes: the xfv_lambda_parity owner-decision queue item (the C-vs-D disagreement dissolved: it was a leak, and the leak-fixed parity protocol loses)
